These are the established Seven Strategic Unclogging Levers introduced in Section 2. The executive team chooses a lever according to the confirmed condition and the specific obstruction to be removed. The S2R® REALIGN stage is the collective decision and ownership step; Lever 06 — Realign is the distinct intervention used to adjust metrics and rewards.
Select the relevant Unclogging Lever. Choose the intervention that addresses the confirmed clog.
Activate the intervention. Implement the decisions and changes agreed during REALIGN.
Verify performance recovery. Confirm that the obstruction is reducing and that the affected performance measures are moving in the intended direction.
Removing a clog requires evidence that the organisational condition has changed. Sustained improvement is verified through the normal performance review rhythm.
People performance
RESTORE equips individuals to deliver under the changed conditions and verifies the change in their work: decisions taken at the right level, delays falling, rework reducing and problems raised early.
Organisational performance
RESTORE applies the lever to the organisational condition and verifies that the condition has changed: the approval route, the data source, the decision right or the measure now supports the execution of the individuals’ tasks, and the Key Result begins to move.
Into the Unclogging Record: the selected lever, the actions with their owners and completion dates, the evidence of recovery and the date of the next review.
The Unclogging Record holds the outcome of each stage in one place. The executive team completes it as it moves through the cycle, then uses it at each later review to check that the agreed actions are complete and the evidence is moving.
Stage · What the record holds
REVIEW · The performance gap, the evidence from the three lines of sight and the confirmed clog.
REALIGN · The coordinating executive, the contributing executives and the agreed changes for people and organisational performance.
RESTORE · The selected lever, the actions with their owners and completion dates, the evidence of recovery and the date of the next review.
The worked example in 4.3 ends with a completed Unclogging Record.

slides.title: 4.3 · Worked example: the Unclogging Cycle
slides.notes:
4.3 — WORKED EXAMPLE: THE UNCLOGGING CYCLE (A manufacturing case)

TEACHING NOTES:
Walk the example step by step: the evidence table of REVIEW, the leadership decisions of REALIGN with the people and organisational implications, the activation of Streamline in RESTORE and the four verification measures. Close on the Completed Unclogging Record.
Then guide participants to apply the same process to their Capstone organisation in Section 5.

Content:
Enterprise Objective. Improve production reliability and on-time customer delivery.
Enterprise Key Result. Increase customer orders delivered on time from 72% to 95% by year-end.
Performance figures are illustrative. The executive team notices that production interruptions are contributing to late deliveries.
Step 1 — REVIEW: Confirm the Performance Clog
Line of sight · Diagnostic finding
Performance Outcome · Only 72% of customer orders are delivered on time, against the 95% target.
Performance Behaviour · Maintenance managers wait for approval before ordering routine replacement parts. Equipment repairs and production schedules are delayed.
Performance Condition · Financial approval requirements place routine maintenance decisions at senior management level, slowing necessary purchases.
Identified clog. Decision Bottlenecks.
The team confirms that avoidable approval delays contribute to maintenance downtime and late customer deliveries.
Step 2 — REALIGN: Agree on Collective Ownership
The CFO and COO agree that routine maintenance decisions must be faster while appropriate financial controls remain in place.
Leadership decision · Agreed response
What must change? · Approval authority for routine maintenance expenditure.
Who coordinates? · CFO — revise financial approval arrangements.
Who contributes? · COO — define operational requirements and ensure adoption.
What must be agreed? · Delegated thresholds, control requirements, responsibilities and an implementation date.
People performance implication
Maintenance managers gain clear authority to purchase approved routine replacement parts and can act promptly within defined controls.
Organisational performance implication
The approval system preserves financial oversight while enabling reliable equipment maintenance and uninterrupted production flow.
Step 3 — RESTORE: Activate the Unclogging Lever
Selected lever. Lever 02 — Streamline | Increase Speed.
Streamline simplifies workflows and removes approval layers that add no value to execution. It is appropriate because the confirmed clog is Decision Bottlenecks, and routine maintenance purchases are delayed by unnecessary approval steps.
Activation. The CFO and COO implement the following changes:
Identify approval steps that cause avoidable delays to routine maintenance purchases.
Remove redundant approvals and simplify the routine purchase workflow.
Retain appropriate controls and senior approval for exceptional or higher-risk expenditure.
Communicate and implement the streamlined process with maintenance and operational teams.
People performance after Streamline
Maintenance managers can obtain routine replacement parts promptly and fulfil their responsibilities within clear approval limits, without repeated unnecessary escalation.
Organisational performance after Streamline
Reduced approval time lowers maintenance downtime, supports production continuity and helps restore on-time customer delivery while preserving financial control.
Verification. At the agreed executive review, examine:
Routine maintenance approval turnaround time.
Equipment downtime caused by delayed replacement parts.
On-time customer delivery performance.
Compliance with the revised financial controls.
The intervention is working when maintenance managers can exercise the revised authority confidently, routine decisions are made faster, approval-related downtime falls and customer delivery performance begins to recover without weakening financial control.
Completed Unclogging Record
S2R® discipline · Leadership record
REVIEW · Decision Bottlenecks are contributing to maintenance and production delays.
REALIGN · CFO coordinates; COO contributes. Both agree on revised approval authority and controls.
RESTORE · Activate Lever 02 — Streamline and verify improvement through approval time, downtime, delivery and financial-control evidence.

TEACHING NOTES:

Content:
Before the group finalises its response, it tests the response against four criteria:

The selected clog names the underlying organisational condition behind the symptom.

slides.title: Unit Summary · Closing
slides.notes:
UNIT SUMMARY (Unit 9 synthesis)

Content:
Awareness — What
A Strategic Clog is an internal blockage that prevents strategic intent from flowing into execution. Clogs form where the strategy stretches today’s organisation. Performance has two connected dimensions, organisational performance and people performance. The 7-Clog Diagnostic Map, aligned to ABCV Directional Integrity, examines both, and the Three Performance Lines of Sight trace a result from its outcome to the behaviours and the conditions behind it.
Intelligence — Why
Leaders resolve clogs through three disciplines: early identification, accurate classification and targeted intervention. The 7 Strategic Unclogging Levers act on people performance and organisational performance together.
Extrapolating — Where
Every executive function shapes the conditions in which other teams work. Traced through the Three Performance Lines of Sight, a decision or practice in one function can create or reinforce a clog in another.
Integration — Collective
Clogs rarely stay in one lane. The leadership team removes them together through the Unclogging Cycle: REVIEW confirms the clog, REALIGN agrees collective ownership and the changes for people and organisational performance, and RESTORE activates the Unclogging Lever and verifies recovery. Each stage completes part of the Unclogging Record.
Application — In Practice
Each group selected a challenge from its Problem Charter, identified the clog, selected the lever and simulated the Unclogging Cycle within its Capstone organisation. The agreed record feeds the team’s Capstone Blueprint.
“When unclogging becomes a habit, everything changes. Friction is a signal telling you how the organisation needs to evolve next. You start engineering flow.”
◆ Facilitator Closing Note
Close by asking each leader to name one clog that has been present in their organisation for more than six months — visible, discussed, but not yet cleared. Ask them: “What has it actually cost the organisation in strategic momentum? And what is the real reason it hasn’t been cleared yet?” The answers to the second question are almost always the true clogs beneath the clogs. That conversation is the beginning of genuine execution engineering. Remind participants that the group’s confirmed Section 5 record feeds the team’s Capstone Blueprint.

Professional insights:

Old breaches: Some present problems are the bill for a past breach. When a recurring problem resists treatment, investigate what older, unsettled matter it may be surfacing.

Stepping over: A dangerous cultural failure is high-performing indifference: people who step over a problem every day without registering it as theirs to solve. Put it on the agenda before the stepping-over becomes the culture.
